title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 33
paragraphs: After this he made preparations for marching to Abydos; and in the meantime the Hellespont was being bridged from Asia to Europe. Now in the Chersonese of the Hellespont, between the city of Sestos and Madytus, there is a broad headland running down into the sea directly opposite Abydos. This is the place where, not long afterwards, the Athenians under the command of Xanthippus son of Ariphron, having captured a Persian named Artayctes, the governor of Sestos, nailed him alive to a plank with hands and feet outstretched. He was the man who used to take women with him into the temple of Protesilaus at Elaeus and do unlawful things there.
